researchTitle: Kuhni ECR industrial and pilot scale-up audit
scope: separation of observed data, explicit limits, and recommendations

decision.label: major scale-up extrapolation, not invalid
basis: target is 4.56 times the largest 152 mm apparatus located in the cited records
current compartment-height ratio is 0.50, outside the cited 0.20-0.30 Kühni recommendation
Perry recommends a 60 mm pilot for specifying columns up to 1 m, so the target is not prohibited
Sulzer lists industrial ECR diameters through 3.5 m, but that is a product envelope rather than a correlation-validity limit

sources.title: Kühni agitated columns (ECR)
evidence: diameter 30 mm-3.5 m
typical industrial speed 10-100 rpm
geometry can be adapted for changing hydrodynamic conditions
reliable scale-up is a product characteristic
sources.limitations: Not a universal correlation-validity range, hard maximum, or target-specific pilot validation.

sources.title: OptimEXT: Advanced solutions for extraction and solvent recovery, E10556 en 5.2025
evidence: p. 4: ECR diameter 30 mm-3.5 m; typical industrial speed 10-70 rpm
p. 4: turbine diameter, turbine height, partition-plate open area, and compartment height are adjustable geometry parameters
p. 8: agitated pilot columns 32, 60, and 150 mm
p. 8: pilot trials precede scale-up and design
p. 9: simple empirical methods normally fail; hydrodynamics and mass transfer support scale-up
sources.limitations: Vendor brochure; pilot sizes are available equipment, not commercial diameter limits.

sources.title: Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook, 8th ed., Section 15, Agitated Extraction Columns
sources.citation: McGraw-Hill, 2008, printed p. 15-83; generic stirred-vessel scale-up discussion p. 15-88 and following
evidence: compartment height 0.20-0.30 Dt
stator fractional free area 0.20-0.40
60 mm pilot for specifying columns up to 1 m
150 mm pilot for specifying larger-diameter columns
some pilot testing recommended for final commercial design
free area trade-off: throughput versus axial mixing and mass-transfer performance
individual stage geometry and free area may be tailored
sources.classification: explicit published recommendation and design guidance
sources.limitations: Copyrighted handbook; the 60/150 mm mapping is a recommendation, not an observed limit or guarantee. Generic p. 15-88 power/tip criteria are not Kühni-specific.

sources.title: Mass transfer and axial dispersion in a Kühni extraction column
evidence: 72.45 mm diameter
25 stages
MIBK-water-acetic acid
concentration profiles, backmixing, and mass transfer
sources.limitations: The apparatus diameter is not a maximum-validity statement.

sources.title: Measurement of Drop Rise Velocities within a Kühni Extraction Column
evidence: 25-stage 72.45 mm precision-bore glass column
50 mm stator plate spacing
sources.limitations: Publisher abstract/metadata is accessible; full article is paywalled. No universal diameter or speed limit is inferred.

sources.title: Performance Map for the Design of Liquid-Liquid Extraction Columns
sources.citation: Chemie Ingenieur Technik 91 (2019) 1674-1680, Section 2.1/Table 1 and Section 3.4
evidence: Garthe DN80 Kühni column
column height 2.95 m
compartment height 50 mm
rotor diameter 45 mm
stator free cross section 40%
150 and 200 rpm operation points
sources.classification: secondary report of pilot experiment and model comparison
sources.limitations: It documents one DN80 apparatus and selected speeds, not the complete Garthe thesis apparatus inventory.

sources.title: Digital Extraction Column: Measurement and Modeling Techniques
evidence: review table includes Kühni D=152 mm turbine-agitator studies
review table also includes D=32 mm Kühni studies
sources.limitations: Reported apparatus sizes are not upper limits or scale-up guarantees.

sources.title: Fluiddynamics and Mass Transfer of Single Particles and Swarms of Particles in Extraction Columns
sources.citation: Daniel Garthe, PhD thesis, Technische Universität München, accepted 2006-04-03; cited as reference 5 by Weber et al. (2019)
evidence: Printed p. 86 Eq. 5.6: Kühni characteristic-velocity correlation with geometry, drop-size, free-area, and power-number terms
Printed p. 126 Eq. 8.3: v_s/v_o = sqrt(C_D,o(Re_o)/C_D,o(Re_s)*(1-h_d)^4.65)
Rendered screenshots .agents/outputs/garthe-eq83-correct/pdf-page-138-printed-126.png and eq83-radical-crop.png confirm the radical spans the complete product, including the holdup factor
Printed Figure 5.20: 143 Kühni points, 10.7% relative error, and listed ranges D_C=72-152 mm, d_A=41-85 mm, d_s=47.5-83.2 mm, n_R=50-250 rpm, d=0.9-6.4 mm
Printed p. 86 discussion: compartment height and stator design should be separately investigated
sources.classification: inspected primary source; local extraction and page rendering
sources.limitations: Printed Figure 5.20 ranges are a correlation/data envelope, not a commercial maximum or universal scale-up rule. Rendered Eq. 8.3 matches the current resolver's inside-radical swarm closure.

unverifiedClaims.claim: Garthe experimental D=72-152 mm and RPM=50-250
unverifiedClaims.status: verified as the ranges listed with Figure 5.20 in the inspected local primary PDF
unverifiedClaims.safeTreatment: Report as a printed Garthe correlation/data envelope, not as a commercial maximum or universal validity boundary; distinguish it from the selected DN80/150-200 rpm secondary report.

scaleUpInvariants.geometryRatios: Explicit recommended Kühni ranges are available.
scaleUpInvariants.statorFreeArea: Not a demonstrated invariant; free area is adjustable and stage-specific tailoring is reported.
scaleUpInvariants.powerPerVolume: Generic agitated-vessel criterion in Perry, not an explicit Kühni-specific invariant in the cited passage.
scaleUpInvariants.tipSpeed: Generic agitated-vessel criterion in Perry, not an explicit Kühni-specific invariant in the cited passage.
scaleUpInvariants.characteristicVelocity: Cited primary, handbook, and Sulzer sources publish correlations and geometry guidance, but no explicit fixed characteristic-velocity scale-up invariant was located.
